analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Record stock market in Stockholm and a budget without reforms
key_insights: Risk appetite returned on 11 Nov after CoreWeave's report eased AI investment concerns following this week's Nvidia slump. Nasdaq +1.6%, S&P 500 +1.3%. Futures point to a lower open on 12 Nov.
Stockholm stock exchange rose a third straight day, +1.0% to a record high. It is up 17% year to date, 7 percentage points more than in an average year.
Oil rose to around USD 95/bbl on 11 Nov before falling back overnight. Gold, which now trades more like a risk asset, fell below USD 4,000/oz.

CoreWeave raised full-year guidance and expects adjusted profitability in 1H 2028, easing concerns about its debt. Anthropic is reported to be considering a higher IPO valuation after record demand. The AI market is described as an important macro issue because of its financial and economic impact.

Abu Dhabi talks (two days) produced no breakthrough on territory, security guarantees or a ceasefire. The parties agreed in principle on a larger prisoner exchange, with scope to be finalised 12 Nov. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner travel to meet Putin 12 Nov.

UK Q3 GDP consensus is 0.7% q/q. A strong print would fit SEB's 1.4% forecast for 2026 and help ease pressure on public finances ahead of 2027, when the economy is expected to turn down and major budget issues must be settled. Much of this year's growth is attributed to AI, mainly through building and developing the technology.

Spain held its first general strike in 14 years on 11 Nov, with housing as the main issue. The same issue triggered the snap election on 29 November. The Socialists trail in polls and the People's Party with Vox could win an outright majority. SEB does not expect the election to affect growth significantly.

Norwegian oil investment survey due 08:00. The previous survey lifted 2027 plans sharply to NOK 227bn after three new development plans, but that is still just over 17% below this year's level. Investment is expected to decline next year with few new projects in the pipeline.

Sweden's 2027 caretaker budget (Finance Minister Svantesson) mainly extends earlier decisions with no new reforms. A planned SEK 1.5bn research boost and higher vocational education expansion are on hold. Other parties have until 27 November to submit counter-proposals, and the Tidö parties have not ruled out a budget of their own.

The Swedish 2-year yield rose 14bp over two days, driven mainly by repricing toward a hawkish Fed and by the Riksbank minutes. SEB sees limited scope for a further rise as the Riksbank's position looks better. First Deputy Governor Bunge speaks at 13:15, and final October inflation is expected to confirm the low flash estimate.
earnings_insights: CoreWeave raised full-year guidance (company guidance, already reported) and expects adjusted profitability in 1H 2028.

SEB's relatively optimistic forecast, needed to ease pressure on public finances ahead of 2027.
Level from the previous survey, just over 17% below this year's. The peak appears to have passed.
Driven mainly by repricing toward a hawkish Fed and by the Riksbank minutes. Further upside seen as limited.
The flash estimate was a low inflation outcome. Bunge's speech tests whether the minutes' hawkish tone holds.

UK public finances face a tougher 2027 as the economy turns down and major budget issues must be settled.
Global rates, including a hawkish Fed repricing, can push Swedish yields higher.
Swedish budget: the Tidö parties have not ruled out a budget of their own, and counter-proposals are due by 27 November.
